title: U.S. House · Florida's 27th District
area: Coastal Miami-Dade County, including Miami, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne and the Florida Keys' northern portion.

context.text: Incumbent Maria Elvira Salazar won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 81.3% of the vote over V. Michael Arias. Eliott Rodriguez won the Democratic primary with 53.5% of the vote over Robin Peguero.

candidates.name: Maria Elvira Salazar
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 81.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Maria Elvira Salazar is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to represent Florida's 27th District, a seat she has held since 2021. She is a former television journalist and news anchor.

background.text: Born in Miami, Florida, in 1961; earned an undergraduate degree in communications from the University of Miami (1983) and a master's in public administration from Harvard University (1995).
Worked as a television journalist, reporter and news anchor before entering politics.

priorities.text: Is the lead sponsor of the DIGNITY Act, which she describes as combining border security and rule-of-law enforcement with legal status for long-term undocumented residents.
priorities.quote: A nation can defend its borders without closing its heart. We can uphold the rule of law, demand responsibility, and protect our country while recognizing the inherent dignity of every person and the reality of families who have lived, worked, worshiped, and built their lives here for years.

priorities.text: Says addressing the housing shortage by removing regulatory barriers to building homes is a priority, citing her work on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and RESIDE Act.
priorities.quote: At the heart of America's housing crisis is a simple problem: we are not building enough homes.

priorities.text: As Chairwoman of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, says increasing financial and diplomatic pressure on the Cuban and Venezuelan regimes is a priority.

positions.summary: Lead sponsor of the DIGNITY Act, which pairs border security and rule-of-law enforcement with a legal-status pathway for long-term undocumented residents; also co-leads and signed a discharge petition for the American Dream and Promise Act to provide permanent legal status to Dreamers and TPS recipients.
positions.quote: A nation can defend its borders without closing its heart. We can uphold the rule of law, demand responsibility, and protect our country while recognizing the inherent dignity of every person and the reality of families who have lived, worked, worshiped, and built their lives here for years.

positions.summary: Helped advance the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which removes regulatory barriers to building homes, streamlines housing development approvals, and expands housing supply.
positions.quote: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act takes meaningful steps to address that challenge by making it easier to build, finance, and expand housing opportunities.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, where she chairs the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere and served on the Small Business Committee during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Lead sponsor of the DIGNITY Act (H.R. 4393), a bipartisan immigration bill that had reached 40 congressional cosponsors and more than 100 endorsing organizations as of late 2026.
Republican co-lead of the RESIDE Act, included in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which is intended to help communities convert vacant and abandoned properties into housing.

candidates.researchNotes: Salazar has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script, per this project's division of labor. Her official issues pages (congress, economy, education, energy, health, veterans) contain no substantive text, only a prompt to contact her office, so positions here are drawn from her office's press releases. No statement squarely addressing U.S. military aid to Israel, gun laws, abortion, or taxes on high earners/corporations was found among her press releases checked, so those issues were left out.

candidates.name: Eliott Rodriguez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Eliott Rodriguez is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 27th Congressional District, the son of union workers who later became small-business owners, running on economic, environmental and labor policy issues.

background.text: Says his parents were union workers who later became small-business owners.

priorities.text: Economy: supports fair market competition and requiring wealthy individuals and large corporations to pay what he calls their fair share, while opposing government ownership stakes in private businesses.
South Florida environment: investing in Everglades restoration, clean water, resilient infrastructure and protection of Biscayne Bay, and holding polluters accountable.
Labor: raising the federal minimum wage and enacting laws to protect government and private-sector workers' collective bargaining rights.

positions.summary: Says he will push to increase the federal minimum wage.
Says he will require wealthy individuals and large corporations to pay their fair share without punishing ordinary families or small businesses.
positions.quote: Require wealthy individuals and large corporations to pay their fair share without punishing ordinary families or legitimate small businesses.

positions.summary: Supports expanding cleaner energy while protecting affordability and reliability, and investing in Everglades restoration and resilient infrastructure to address flooding, intense heat and stronger storms.
Supports restoring the federal ban on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, requiring universal background checks, and passing Ethan's Law to require safe firearm storage.
positions.quote: Eliott supports common-sense gun safety measures that protect our children and communities while respecting the rights of responsible gun owners.

candidates.researchNotes: Rodriguez has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and has not previously held elected office; positions are drawn from his campaign website's issues page. His Ballotpedia page includes no independent biography beyond election results.
